checkpoints.prompt: For each request, say where it should be answered (which layer or cache) and whether it is safe to share between users: (1) a 4-second segment of episode 3 in 1080p, requested by 40,000 viewers tonight; (2) CampusPulse's /assets/index-C4c61eeb.js, built by Vite; (3) CampusPulse's /api/status, identical for everyone, changing every few seconds; (4) a streaming app's "Continue watching" row for the signed-in viewer.

Design the cache for two CampusPulse features. For each, name the layer(s), the key, how it is invalidated, and one line of config (header or code): (1) building hours at /api/buildings/hours — same for everyone, edited by staff about once a week, read on every page load; (2) "My reports" at /api/me/reports — a signed-in student's own outage reports, updated when they file one.

Your CampusPulse status page renders in 900 ms but nobody can submit an outage report. Which of these tells you? (1) Lighthouse in CI, scored 98 this morning; (2) an axe run in the pipeline, zero violations; (3) the metric http_requests_total{route="/incidents",status="2xx"}; (4) an uptime check hitting /healthz every 60 s. Then write one SLO for your own CampusPulse: it must name a user-visible action, a threshold, a percentage, a window, and say whether it is request-based or time-based.
